Lumen: styleguide

Lumen is the Taiga framework for showcase products: cinematic, high-contrast, glass-driven interfaces that present results to people, tell a story, or run a studio. This guide is extracted from the four Lumen codebases. It describes what they actually do, with the values they actually use, and turns that into rules for future projects.

App What it is Canonical stylesheet(s) Default theme
QuantSkill 2.3.0 Adaptive skills assessment (Shiny · Quarto · HTML) srcjs/css/quantskill.css Daylight (light), true-black dark
lumenJourney 0.3.0 Clinical study story (Shiny · Quarto · HTML · PDF) + a teal app inst/story/lumen-story.css Cinema (dark), paper light
DirectoR 0.1.3 Studio that directs launch films for apps inst/app/www/director.css (+ inst/engine/stage/stage.css) Studio dark only
RockShiny 0.1.0 Note-highway music player inst/app/app.css, inst/highway/highway.css Stage dark only

Numbers in this guide come from tools/extract_tokens.py (→ tokens/*.json, tokens/summary.md) and tools/contrast_audit.py (→ tokens/contrast.md). Re-run them after the apps change. A starter token sheet for new projects is in lumen-tokens.css.

1. Principles

  1. Cinematic. Every app has a set: a deep canvas (#000, #07070a or #0b0d13) or an off-white one (#fbfbfd, paper #f8f7f3). Ambient light comes from slow radial glows, and a headline is set in display type with a gradient on the key words. Each screen composes like a frame of a film.
  2. High contrast where it counts. Primary text sits at 15:1 to 19:1 against the canvas in every Lumen theme. Hierarchy comes from size, weight and tracking. Muted greys are kept for secondary text.
  3. Glass for everything that floats. Navigation, docks, HUDs, cards over content and sheets are translucent (about 72 % opaque), blurred (10–22 px) and saturated (140–180 %), with a hairline border. Content that sits in the page stays solid.
  4. One accent, one gradient. Each app owns one saturated accent, and optionally one gradient, used for primary actions, focus and highlighted words. Semantic colours (good, warn, bad) never double as brand colour.
  5. Motion tells the story. Entrances rise, numbers count up, scroll drives narrative (journey steps, radar morphs), and springy feedback confirms actions. Motion always has a still fallback.
  6. Self-contained. Every Lumen front end is a dependency-free bundle: no CDN, no framework, and fonts inlined or from the system. This is what allows the triple-format delivery (../DELIVERY_MODEL.md).

2.3 Ambient light

  • Blobs (QuantSkill .qs-blob): three 60 vmax circles (#2563eb, #a855f7, #f97316), filter: blur(90px), opacity .22 (.30 dark), drifting over 26, 30 and 34 s alternate loops. They dim to .12 in focus mode.
  • Glows (DirectoR body.dr::before): three radial gradients (indigo .16, purple .13, pink .09) drifting over 30 s.
  • Bokeh (story .ls-bokeh): twelve coloured dots (RGB triplets above) that rise in and drift.
  • Grain: an SVG feTurbulence overlay at 3.5 % opacity (.qs-grain).
  • Stage (RockShiny): one fixed radial gradient (#1a2035 → #0b0d13), with no animation so the highway stays readable.

Ambient layers are position: fixed, pointer-events: none, z-index: -1 or 0, and must be switched off or frozen for screenshots and video capture (QuantSkill’s recorder replaces blurs with look-alike masks; see §6.3).

2.4 Contrast rules (from tokens/contrast.md)

Pair Ratio Rule
Text 1 on canvas (all themes) 15.6 – 19.3 Body text, headings: always.
Text 2 on canvas 4.9 – 8.2 (QuantSkill light on --bg-3: 4.30) Secondary text. Not on --bg-3 fills for small text.
Text 3 on canvas 3.1 – 4.1 (story paper: 3.17; DirectoR --dim: 4.00) Large text (≥ 24 px, or ≥ 18.7 px bold), captions next to a stronger label, placeholders. Never the only carrier of information.
White on QuantSkill dark accent #0a84ff 3.65 Large or bold button labels only (the 17 px, 550 weight .is-lg buttons).
White on DirectoR --a1 / --a2 4.47 / 3.96 The gradient button needs ≥ 15 px semibold (it uses 13.5–15 px, 600): keep labels short and bold.

New projects must keep text 3 for large or decorative text only, and check every accent they use for filled buttons against white (≥ 4.5:1 for 14 px labels).

Display clamp(52px, 9.2vw, 112px), weight 700, lh .98, tracking −.045em hero clamp(44px, 8.4vw, 104px), −.045em hero clamp(40px, 5.6vw, 76px), weight 780, −.05em brand 1.15 rem, 800
H1 / H2 clamp(36px, 5vw, 56px) / clamp(32px, 4.6vw, 56px), −.035em section title clamp(40px, 6vw, 72px), −.04em page head 28 px, 750, −.035em card title 16 px, 750
Lede clamp(18px, 2vw, 22px), lh 1.42 clamp(19px, 2.2vw, 24px), lh 1.4 17 px (.sublead) –
Eyebrow / caps .qs-eyebrow 13 px, 600, +.02em, sentence case .ls-kicker 12 px caps, 600, +.06em (paper theme: eyebrows 13 px caps, 500, +.14em) eyebrow = pill with a gradient “NEW” badge (11 px, 650); step labels 11 px caps, 700, +.08em brand sub .72rem caps, +.12em

Rules:

  • Display type is tight and heavy. Use −.035em to −.05em tracking and weight 700–780, with line-height ≤ 1.05. Set the key words in the gradient (background-clip: text), never the whole line.
  • Weights in use (by frequency): 600, 650, 700 and 750 for UI; 500–550 for buttons; 400 for body. The story’s paper theme is the exception. It is editorial, not cinematic: hero title 200, titles and leads 300, stat numbers 200 with lining tabular numerals.
  • Numbers. font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums for stats, timers and scores (.ls-stat-num, .ls-tile-big).
  • Fonts never come from a CDN. DirectoR ships Inter, QuantSkill relies on the system stack, and QuantSkill’s video pipeline inlines Inter as base64.

4. Shape, elevation and glass

4.1 Radii

Token QuantSkill lumenJourney DirectoR RockShiny
XL (sheets, hero cards) --r-xl 34px --ls-radius 28px (paper 22) – 18 px
L (cards) --r-l 26px 22–24 px --r 16px 14–16 px
M (controls, tiles) --r-m 18px 14 px --r2 12px 12 px
S (chips, inputs) --r-s 12px 8–10 px --r3 10px, buttons 11 px 10 px / .55rem
Pill 999px (buttons, chips, nav links) 999px 999px (chips) 999px

Buttons are pills in QuantSkill and the story, and rounded rectangles (11 px) in DirectoR. Choose one per app. Never mix the two for the same action level.

4.2 Shadows

  • Daylight (QuantSkill): --shadow-1: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.04), 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.06), --shadow-2: 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.05), 0 30px 70px rgba(0,0,0,.13).
  • Night: the same geometry at .4–.6 alpha. DirectoR --shadow: 0 24px 60px -24px rgba(0,0,0,.7), 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.04) inset (an inner top highlight makes dark cards read as glass).
  • Coloured glow for primary actions: 0 10px 28px -10px rgba(168,85,247,.85) (DirectoR) or 0 6px 20px -6px color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 70%, transparent) (QuantSkill). The glow grows on hover.

4.3 The glass recipe

.glass {
  background: var(--card);                            /* ~72% opaque surface colour */
  backdrop-filter: blur(20px) saturate(170%);         /* 10-22px blur, 140-180% saturate */
  -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(20px) saturate(170%);
  border: 1px solid var(--line);                      /* hairline, 8-10% */
  box-shadow: var(--shadow-1);
}
@supports not ((backdrop-filter: blur(1px)) or (-webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(1px))) {
  .glass { background: var(--card-solid); }           /* lumenJourney ships this fallback */
}
Where glass is used Blur / saturate
Sticky nav after scroll (QuantSkill .is-scrolled .qs-nav, story .ls-nav) saturate(180%) blur(20px)
Quiz top bar and answer dock (QuantSkill) blur(20px) saturate(170%)
Cards over ambient light (.qs-card, .qs-results-overall) blur(20px) saturate(160%)
Studio rail and top bar (DirectoR) blur(20px), blur(18px)
Highway HUD: song card, section pill, transport (RockShiny) blur(10px) saturate(140%)
Modals and scrims blur(6–8px) over rgba(0,0,0,.35)

Counts from the stylesheets: QuantSkill 18 and lumenJourney 18 backdrop-filter declarations, DirectoR 8, RockShiny 4. Glass is a signature, not a texture: only surfaces that float over moving or layered content get it.

5. Motion

Token Value Use
--ease (--ls-ease) cubic-bezier(.2, .8, .2, 1) Default for everything. Used 27× in QuantSkill, 48× in the story, 2× plus variants in DirectoR.
--spring cubic-bezier(.34, 1.56, .64, 1) Confirmations: buttons, icons, badges, logo hover (32× in QuantSkill).
DirectoR spring cubic-bezier(.2, .9, .3, 1.4) Logo and choice-card pop.
Fast .2s – .25s Hover, colour, background.
Medium .3s – .55s Entrances (qs-view-in, pgIn .45 s), sheets.
Slow .7s – 1.1s Hero rise (ls-rise 1.1 s), count-ups (900 ms cubic out).
Ambient 26 – 34 s alternate Blobs and glows.

Signature animations: qs-view-in / pgIn (rise 10–16 px and fade); view transitions (::view-transition-old/new(qs-main)); count-up numbers; scroll-driven story steps (the journey’s dot grid re-sorts per step); qs-correct, qs-shake and qs-medal feedback; confetti for achievements; the studio’s transition demos (trFade, trWipe, trIris…).

Rules:

  • Every animation has a still state. QuantSkill and the story implement @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce). DirectoR and RockShiny do not yet (see requirements).
  • Capture-friendly. Animations are CSS or Web Animations so a recorder can pause and seek them (QuantSkill’s recorder.py freezes every animation on start and advances it frame by frame), and Math.random is only used where a seeded replacement is acceptable.

6.1 Z-order (observed)

Ambient −1 → content → sticky nav 50 → overlays 60–100 → toasts 200–300 → capture layers 100001+.

6.2 Print

The story ships 11 print rules (a journal-style article) and QuantSkill 2 (its PDF report is generated separately). Long-form Lumen pages should print cleanly: ambient light and glass off, solid surfaces, page breaks between sections.

6.3 Capture

Screenshots and videos are first-class deliverables of a Lumen app (QuantSkill and DirectoR exist partly to make them). Keep heavy effects switchable: QuantSkill’s recorder injects CAPTURE_CSS (blobs unblurred, grain hidden, card blurs removed) so frames render fast and identically.

7.2 Anatomy of the shared patterns

  • Primary button. A pill (or 11 px radius) 40–50 px tall with a 15–17 px, 550–600 label, filled with the accent or gradient, a coloured glow shadow, and a trailing icon that nudges +3 px on hover. :active scales to .96–.97.
  • Glass HUD card. Absolute inside a stage, 14 px from the edges: 12 px radius, --glass, blur 10 px, inset 0 0 0 1px var(--line). Title 16 px/750, meta 12 px muted, tags as 999 px chips.
  • Choice card (DirectoR dr-choices.cards). A grid with --min column width, each card holding a visual (.vis), a title (.t) and a subline (.s). Active: gradient-tinted background, a purple inset ring and a check badge.
  • Chip. 26 px (QuantSkill) or 4 × 10 px padding (DirectoR), 999 px radius, 12–12.5 px/550–600. Variants accent, good, warn, bad tint the border and a 6–12 % background.
  • Big number tile. Tabular numerals, display tracking, a unit in muted small type, and a mini chart (bar, dots or sparkline) underneath.

8. App dialects

  • QuantSkill: Daylight glass. Light by default, Apple-like neutrals, drifting blobs, glass cards, pills, per-area category colours, gamification (XP, streaks, badges, confetti), view transitions. True-black dark theme.
  • lumenJourney: Cinema story. Dark by default (data-theme="dark"), full-bleed chapters, gradient hero, count-ups, one-dot-per-patient storytelling, a floating glass filter pill. The paper light theme (#f8f7f3, Helvetica Neue, hairline shadows --ls-hair) is the print-like editorial variant.
  • DirectoR: Studio dark. Dark only, Inter, white-alpha panels, an indigo → purple → pink gradient for brand and primary actions, a left rail with glowing active state, rich choice cards with live visual previews.
  • RockShiny: Stage dark. A bslib theme (bg #0b0d13, fg #e8eaf1, primary #f5a524) around an immersive canvas. Chrome is quiet, the stage is loud (instrument colours), and the HUD floats as glass on the stage.
Glass tiles, big numbers Paper theme Studio: cards + live preview Stage: HUD + loop

9. Do and don’t

Do Don’t
Start from a deep or off-white canvas and add one ambient layer. Put glass on content that does not float.
Put the gradient on 1–3 key words of a display line. Gradient whole paragraphs, buttons and headings on one screen.
Keep text 1 for anything the reader must read. Use text 3 (3–4:1) for body copy or data labels.
Give every animation a reduced-motion still. Tie meaning to motion alone (counting numbers end on the true value).
Ship fonts and assets inside the bundle. Load fonts, icons or scripts from a CDN.
Make heavy effects switchable for capture and print. Let backdrop-filter stack more than two layers deep.
Use domain colours (strings, arms, areas) from code constants. Reuse semantic red and green as brand colours.
